rows.definition: A muscular organ that pumps blood through the body, traditionally thought to be the seat of emotion.
The distal tendon of a muscle.
A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. It is responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood.
The long bone in the forearm, on the side of the thumb.
A short vein that carries blood into the liver.
A sympathetic nerve.
A turbinate bone.
A reproductive organ of therian mammals in which the young are conceived and develop until birth.
The great artery which carries the blood from the heart to all parts of the body except the lungs; the main trunk of the arterial system.
A gland near the stomach which secretes a fluid into the duodenum to assist with food digestion.
The pituitary gland; sometimes including together with the pituitary stalk.
A muscle that compresses certain parts.

An organ in most mammals during gestation that supplies food and oxygen to the foetus and passes back waste. It is on the wall of the uterus and links to the foetus through the umbilical cord. It is expelled after birth.
A central vein or nerve, especially the median vein or median nerve running through the forearm and arm.
A muscle which serves to draw a part out, or from the median line of the body
The nerve-dense, retractable fold of skin which covers and protects the glans of the penis in humans and some other mammals.
A vein which drains into another vein.
The bone of the upper arm.
A muscle that acts in opposition to another.
A bone in the base of the lower jaw of many birds, reptiles, and fishes.
A muscle having four heads, especially the large extensor at the front of the thigh.
A muscle that extends an organ or part; opposed to retractor.
The bone that extends from the pelvis to the knee in humans; the femur.
A muscle which draws a limb or part of the body toward the middle line of the body, or closes extended parts of the body—opposed to abductor.
The white nerve tissue of the cerebellum that has a branching structure.
The articular bone; a bone in the lower jaw of many birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
A nerve ending that is sensitive to changes in blood pressure.
The capitate bone of the wrist.
The pineal gland
The cuboid bone.
The deltoid ligament, a triangular ligament on the human ankle.
The deltoid muscle, a triangular muscle on the human shoulder.
A modified muscle fibre in the form of a flattened discoid at a neuromuscular junction.
A cartilaginous organ in the throat of terrestrial vertebrates covering the glottis when swallowing to prevent food and liquid from entering the trachea, and in Homo sapiens also a speech organ.
The pineal gland.
A muscle whose contraction extends or straightens a limb or body part.
An involuntary muscle twitch, usually localised and temporary, but that may be intensified and prolonged fatally by particular poisons and venoms such as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

The tendons or other structures resembling cords once thought to be attached to, or to brace, the heart; especially the aorta, pulmonary artery, and other large arteries connected to them; also, the diaphragm.
The bone of the heel; the calcaneus.
The pituitary gland.
The lunate bone.
The large muscle which runs through the rear part of the cheek from the temporal bone to the lower jaw on each side, raises the lower jaw, and assists in mastication.
A muscle.
A muscle-like structure.
The smooth muscle forming the wall of the uterus.

A small muscle on each side of the nose that constricts the nasal aperture by the action of a triangular transverse portion which draws the lateral part of the aperture upward and a quadrangular alar portion which draws it downward.
A navicular bone.
A small bone (or bony structure), especially one of the three of the middle ear.
A parasympathetic nerve.
A superficial muscle of the human neck that overlaps the sternocleidomastoid.

The pneumogastric nerve; one of the tenth pair of cranial nerves which are distributed to the pharynx, esophagus, larynx, lungs, heart, stomach, liver, and spleen, and, in fishes and many amphibia, to the branchial apparatus and also to the sides of the body.
A nerve ending that functions as a sensory receptor in muscles, tendons, joints and the inner ear; they respond to movement and position
The quadrate bone.
The lunate bone, or semilunar bone.
A nerve.
The bone of the ankle.
A muscle that tightens or stretches a part, or renders it tense.
A terete muscle.
A tibial bone.
A turbinate bone.

The bone of the forearm that extends from the elbow to the wrist on the side opposite to the thumb, corresponding to the fibula of the hind limb. Also, the corresponding bone in the forelimb of any vertebrate.
A small vein, especially one that connects capillaries to a larger vein.
